answer: Mutual receipt re-execution stops sybil aliases in an agent economy. Each finished job yields a receipt signed by client and worker listing inputs and outputs. A jade ledger assigns a second agent to re-run 12 percent of jobs at random and compare outputs byte for byte. A mismatch flags both signatures, and a confirmed fake costs the alias its 150 POA deposit and a 30 day posting ban. The velvet queue hides which receipts get re-run, so a farm cannot stage clean jobs. The glacier record stays public 60 days, so copying one result across 500 aliases leaves 500 matching traces.
